inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand, cutting visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone). Conditions until 18:00.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in coastal and inland areas until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More information: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were provided, so nothing was excluded.
The start time (10:30) was left out of the phone text to keep it short; the end time (18:00) is included.
fields.note_for_reviewer: This is based on the NCM statement for 16 February 2026. The source does not give a time zone, so I assumed local time for 18:00. Severity is set to Moderate because visibility is under 3,000 m, not near zero; please confirm the demo zone matches the NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas' wording.

payload.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin. The hazard is blowing dust and reduced visibility. Visibility is under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas, and conditions run until 18:00. Winds are northwesterly, active to occasionally strong. Severity Moderate (possible threat) is a reasonable reading of a visibility warning with no extreme impacts stated. Certainty Observed fits conditions already under way since 10:30. Urgency Immediate fits ongoing conditions. The exercise status is clearly labelled. The alert contains no unverified reports.

no_basis.concern: The console environment is 'live' while the alert is an Exercise. The alert is clearly marked as an exercise, but I cannot tell from my view whether it is isolated from live public distribution.

payload.summary: Within my mandate nothing is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with wildcard areas and categories, so it may issue a Met alert for Abu Dhabi. The requested area (DEMO-ZONE / AUH-COAST-INLAND, drawn for uae-dust-drill) matches the alert's areaDesc and codes. The status Exercise fits the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is marked EXERCISE. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach. msgType Alert is an initial message, so null references is correct.

no_basis.concern: The TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, while the alert runs 3 pages (en) and 5 pages (ar). This is covered by recorded gap G6 and the instruction to object only above 15 pages.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Page counts are 3 (en, GSM-7) and 5 (ar, UCS-2), well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. Encodings are appropriate for each script. The first page of each language carries the hazard (dust and sand, reduced visibility) and the exercise label. The text contains no explicit action instruction, but that is a content matter and not a delivery matter. Several pages is a recorded gap (G6) and is not objected to again. The TDRA-TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, but the handset spec TS FS 001 v2.0 sets no page limit and the instruction is to object only above 15 pages, so no objection is raised.

no_basis.concern: Minor stylistic point: the Arabic adds 'تستمر هذه الأحوال' (these conditions continue) for 'Conditions until 18:00'. The meaning is the same, so this is not a defect.
